test_intent: Verify that a normal user name produces ModerationAction.Allow from the moderation service.
reason: The test uses FakeModerationService where the result is pre-configured via _fakePolicy.SetResult(). The assertion only verifies the adapter returns what the fake was told to return, not any real policy logic. This is a tautology test. The actual user-name validation behavior is already covered by ModerationServiceTests.CheckUserNameAsync_ValidUser_ReturnsAllowAction which exercises the real ModerationService with mocked dependencies.

test_intent: Verify that a suspiciously long user name produces ModerationAction.Report.
reason: Same structural problem as the normal-name test: FakeModerationService.SetResult() pre-configures the outcome, so the test only verifies the adapter passes through a predetermined value. No real policy logic is exercised. The long-name detection behavior is a real contract but is already covered by ModerationServiceTests.CheckUserNameAsync_InvalidUser_ReturnsBanAction which uses the real ModerationService with mocked classifier dependencies.

test_intent: Verify that an extremely long user name produces ModerationAction.Ban.
reason: Identical pattern: FakeModerationService.SetResult() hardcodes the ban result, making the assertion a tautology. The extremely-long-name ban behavior is a real bot contract but is already exercised by ModerationServiceTests.CheckUserNameAsync_InvalidUser_ReturnsBanAction using the real ModerationService with mocked dependencies. No distinct value beyond that test.

test_intent: Verify that passing null to CheckMessageAsync throws ArgumentNullException with correct parameter name.
reason: Tests defensive null-check on a public API surface. The assertion is correct (Assert.ThrowsAsync with ParamName check), but null-argument guards on service methods are trivial and rarely regress. This is compile-time + code review territory. No distinct bot contract beyond general API hygiene. The test adds negligible safety net value.

test_intent: Verify that a message from a banned user produces ModerationAction.Ban.
reason: Same structural problem: FakeModerationService.SetResult() pre-configures the ban outcome, so the test only verifies the adapter returns what the fake was told to return. The banned-user detection behavior is a real contract but is already covered by ModerationServiceTests.CheckMessageAsync_BadMessage_ReturnsBanAction which exercises the real ModerationService with mocked BadMessageManager. The SimpleTests version adds no additional coverage.

test_intent: Verify that BanAndCleanupUserAsync calls both BanUserAsync and DeleteMessageByIdAsync with correct parameters when a message ID is provided.
reason: The test verifies coordination between ban and message deletion through mock verification (Verify calls). While the assertions are meaningful (checking correct BanTypeEnum, chatId, messageId), the test is tightly coupled to ModerationServiceTestFactory internals and uses heavy mock choreography. The behavior is a real bot contract: banning a user and cleaning up their message. A better seam would test this directly at IUserBanService or as a focused contract test with fewer factory dependencies. Rewrite to reduce mock setup noise and verify the actual side-effect sequence more directly.

test_intent: Verify that BanAndCleanupUserAsync only calls BanUserAsync (not DeleteMessageByIdAsync) when no message ID is provided.
reason: Similar to the previous test but for the no-message-id path. Uses mock Verify to confirm DeleteMessageByIdAsync is never called. The behavior is a real contract (conditional message deletion during ban). Same structural issues: heavy mock choreography through ModerationServiceTestFactory. Rewrite as a focused contract test at the UserBanService seam to verify the conditional delete path more directly with less factory overhead.
